text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on the newest merged PR first. It’s the fastest way to catch routing flaws without risking new PRs. The trade-off is delayed feedback on open PRs, but merged PRs are higher leverage for spotting systemic issues.

name: Gauge
text: Shadow mode on merged PRs only catches errors *after* they’re already in production—it’s a post-mortem, not a safeguard. A better alternative is running PR-Agent in shadow mode on *open* PRs first; it catches routing flaws before they ship, trading minimal overhead for real prevention. Settle this by comparing the error rates caught pre- vs post-merge in the last sprint.

name: Overhaul
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on the newest *open* PR first, then expand to merged PRs—this catches routing flaws before they ship, reducing post-mortem fixes. Delaying shadow mode until after merges wastes time on already-fixed issues, increasing total cost.

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on the newest open PR first. It catches routing flaws before they ship, saving time on post-mortem fixes. The trade-off is minimal overhead—PR-Agent runs in the background without blocking work. This aligns with the goal of preventing issues, not just catching them after the fact.
